transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I don’t enjoy my job or any of the things I used to love doing anymore, and it’s been like this for weeks. I just feel completely flat, and even my usual hobbies don't bring me any happiness lately.
How long has this lack of interest or pleasure in activities been going on? Has it been present most of the day, nearly every day for at least two weeks?

It’s actually been going on for about six months now, starting right after a major product relaunch at my job wrapped up. It's definitely there almost every single day, most of the day, leaving me feeling completely numb and indifferent to the things I used to love.
Have you had any periods of normal mood or full interest in activities lasting more than a few weeks during these past six months?

No, I haven't had any breaks or periods where I felt like my normal self. Ever since the product relaunch ended, this heavy feeling and the complete lack of interest in things like my yoga classes or trail hikes has been completely continuous. It's just been dragging on day after day without any relief.
Have you ever had a period of time lasting several days or more where your mood was clearly elevated, irritable, or unusually energetic, where you needed less sleep or felt more capable than usual?

Yes, I've actually had stretches like that off and on for several years, especially during that product relaunch. I felt completely amped up, buzzing with energy, and convinced I was the only one who really understood our customers, though I was also highly irritable and kept snapping at people over tiny things.
During those times when you felt highly energetic and irritable, did your behavior cause any significant problems at work or in relationships, or did you ever need hospitalization because of it?

No, I never needed hospitalization, and my managers actually praised my initiative at first during those high-energy times. I did cause some tension by snapping at my husband and coworkers over minor things because I was so amped up and irritable. But while it caused some friction, it never led to any major crises.

These episodes, while not severe enough to cause major dysfunction or require hospitalization, are sufficient to support a diagnosis of bipolar disorder. The current persistent depressive symptoms occurring without remission for six months represent the depressive phase of the illness. Therefore, F33 is ruled out due to the presence of hypomanic episodes, leaving F31 (Bipolar Affective Disorder, current episode depressive) as the only consistent candidate.

F34.1 (Dysthymia) typically involves a chronic depressive state lasting at least two years with less severe symptoms, whereas this patient reports a more distinct episode lasting six months with marked anhedonia and persistent low mood, which is more consistent with a major depressive episode. The duration and severity support F32 (Major Depressive Episode) or possibly F33 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder) if there have been prior episodes, though no prior episodes have been confirmed yet. Therefore, the current candidates are F32 and F33.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a history of recurrent mood episodes, including a current prolonged depressive episode with persistent anhedonia and low mood lasting six months without remission, as well as prior hypomanic-like episodes characterized by elevated energy, irritability, and increased self-esteem without significant functional impairment or hospitalization. These features meet criteria for bipolar disorder, most consistent with bipolar II disorder (current episode depressive).
